scenes.title: Standards are for the next reader
scenes.intro: Judge whether another person can understand and change the software.

items.label: Responsibility
items.detail: One module has a clear job.
items.anchor: whether a module has a clear responsibility

items.label: Names
items.detail: Names explain intent.
items.anchor: whether names explain intent

items.label: Boundaries
items.detail: Inputs are checked where they enter.
items.anchor: whether inputs are checked at boundaries

items.label: Findability
items.detail: The next person can locate the behavior.
items.anchor: whether the next person can find the behavior

conclusion.text: The system should not depend on the original author’s memory.

scenes.title: A failed save must look like a failure
scenes.intro: Compare the visitor’s impression with what actually happened.

items.label: False success
items.detail: “Thank you” appears even though nothing was saved.
items.anchor: Imagine the inquiry tracker says

items.label: False belief
items.detail: Visitor and owner both think the inquiry exists.
items.anchor: both visitor and owner believe

items.label: Useful diagnostic
items.detail: Say what failed, where, and what may help.
items.anchor: A helpful diagnostic states what failed

items.label: Safe detail
items.detail: Keep passwords and private content out of the message.
items.anchor: without exposing passwords

conclusion.text: The visitor and operator may need different levels of detail.
conclusion.anchor: can contain different levels of detail

scenes.title: Test the edges of the system
scenes.intro: Check where information enters, leaves, and changes state.

items.label: Submission boundary
items.detail: Try valid and invalid inquiries.
items.anchor: try valid and invalid submissions

items.label: Access boundary
items.detail: Try an unauthorized view of private records.
items.anchor: an unauthorized attempt to view records

items.label: Storage boundary
items.detail: Simulate failure using synthetic data.
items.anchor: and a storage failure

items.label: Non-effects
items.detail: Invalid input saves nothing; failure shows no false success.
items.anchor: Test both the result and important non-effects

conclusion.text: Connect each test to the requirement it supports.
conclusion.anchor: explain which requirement each test supports

scenes.title: A slice includes its proof
scenes.intro: A saved revision is useful, but it is not proof by itself.

items.label: Complete slice
items.detail: Change + relevant check + evidence + project record.
items.anchor: A coherent slice includes the change

items.label: Saved revision
items.detail: A commit records a version.
items.anchor: A commit is a saved revision

items.label: Limit of the claim
items.detail: Small commits do not automatically prove behavior.
items.anchor: They are not automatically proof

items.label: Focused verification
items.detail: Preserve unrelated work and run affected checks.
items.anchor: Keep scope and ownership clear

items.label: When to repeat
items.detail: Rerun after changes, failures, or a new concern.
items.anchor: Repeat checks when the underlying code changes

conclusion.text: Repeat verification when earlier evidence may have become stale.
conclusion.anchor: or a new concern justifies it

scenes.title: Four observations, four different claims
scenes.intro: Treat these as distinct evidence types, not an automatic ladder.

items.label: Implemented
items.detail: The capability is present in code.
items.anchor: Implemented means present in the code

items.label: Offline-tested
items.detail: A controlled environment exercised the behavior.
items.anchor: Offline-tested means tested in a controlled environment

items.label: Provider-accepted
items.detail: An outside service accepted a request.
items.anchor: Provider-accepted means an outside service accepted

items.label: Live-observed
items.detail: The intended real-world effect was observed.
items.anchor: Live-observed means the intended real-world effect

conclusion.text: Provider acceptance does not necessarily prove a person received the message.
conclusion.anchor: necessarily prove the intended person received it

callouts.text: A fake provider response proves response handling—not real delivery.
callouts.anchor: a fake email provider returning success

scenes.title: Keep evidence and recovery inspectable
scenes.intro: A review record should reveal both confidence and gaps.

items.label: Evidence note
items.detail: Revision, commands, results, time, sanitized artifacts.
items.anchor: An evidence record identifies the version

items.label: Missing access
items.detail: A blocker or unverified gap—not a pass.
items.anchor: Missing access is a blocker

items.label: Restore earlier state
items.detail: Explain what happens if the change fails.
items.anchor: Ask what happens when a change fails

items.label: Recovery rehearsal
items.detail: Say whether restoration was actually rehearsed.
items.anchor: whether the restoration was actually rehearsed

conclusion.text: Review in proportion to risk and new information.
conclusion.anchor: avoiding repeated full reviews that add cost

scenes.title: Make the code explain its purpose
scenes.intro: Future diagnosis starts with names and responsibilities.

items.label: Six months later
items.detail: A new agent must locate the failing behavior.
items.anchor: six months from now the tracker fails

items.label: Purposeful names
items.detail: saveInquiry / listNewInquiries communicate intent.
items.anchor: Names like saveInquiry and listNewInquiries

items.label: Narrow module
items.detail: Separate validation, storage, email, and presentation.
items.anchor: A module with a narrow responsibility

items.label: Dependency map
items.detail: Show dependencies and side effects.
items.anchor: Ask the agent for a map of dependencies

conclusion.text: Require clarity without prescribing every formatting preference.
conclusion.anchor: require that future readers can follow the system

scenes.title: Give the right person the right error
scenes.intro: Visitor feedback and operator diagnostics serve different jobs.

items.label: Visitor
items.detail: “Enter a way for us to contact you.”
items.anchor: If a required field is missing

items.label: Operator
items.detail: Identify the failed storage component and safe next step.
items.anchor: If the storage service is down

items.label: Privacy boundary
items.detail: Avoid unnecessary contact details and credentials in logs.
items.anchor: Logs should avoid recording sensitive contact details

items.label: Right audience
items.detail: Do not make every diagnostic public.
items.anchor: not to make every error public

conclusion.text: The person responsible should be able to understand and respond.
conclusion.anchor: the right person can understand and respond

scenes.title: Prove the forbidden effects stay absent
scenes.intro: A successful example cannot cover every important boundary.

items.label: Missing contact method
items.detail: Submit an inquiry without a way to reply.
items.anchor: submit an inquiry without a contact method

items.label: No saved record
items.detail: Confirm rejection and absence of a record.
items.anchor: Confirm the system rejects it

items.label: Unauthorized access
items.detail: The owner view denies an unauthorized visitor.
items.anchor: Attempt to open the owner view without authorization

items.label: Failed storage
items.detail: The public form must not show success.
items.anchor: Simulate a storage failure

conclusion.text: Negative checks reveal failures a happy-path demo can miss.

scenes.title: Where was the claim tested?
scenes.intro: Match the environment to the observation.

items.label: Local fake
items.detail: The application handles a simulated response.
items.anchor: A local test may replace a provider

items.label: Real provider
items.detail: Local behavior does not prove account access or delivery.
items.anchor: it cannot prove the real provider accepts

items.label: Real user
items.detail: Acceptance and observed effect are different observations.
items.anchor: A provider's acceptance is a stronger

items.label: Evidence label
items.detail: Record environment, exact claim, and untested gaps.
items.anchor: Record the environment and the exact claim

conclusion.text: “Not yet tested” prevents someone from assuming proof exists.
conclusion.anchor: keeps the next person from assuming proof exists

scenes.title: Review one coherent change
scenes.intro: Ask focused questions while the change is small enough to assess.

items.label: Requirement
items.detail: Which behavior does the change implement?
items.anchor: which requirement does this change implement

items.label: Inputs and failures
items.detail: What is accepted; what happens when it fails?
items.anchor: What inputs does it accept

items.label: Tests and privacy
items.detail: Which checks changed; could private data be exposed?
items.anchor: Which tests changed

items.label: Recovery and documents
items.detail: Can it be reversed, and do the docs still agree?
items.anchor: Is there an obvious rollback

items.label: Freshness
items.detail: Repeat checks when a change makes earlier results stale.
items.anchor: but do run checks again

conclusion.text: Use new evidence when the behavior or risk changes.
conclusion.anchor: a change or failure makes earlier results stale

callouts.text: A small verified change keeps the review questions manageable.
callouts.anchor: verified commit keeps these questions manageable

scenes.title: Write a record someone else can inspect
scenes.intro: A useful evidence note contains context rather than confidence alone.

items.label: Revision + local suite
items.detail: Record which revision and cases passed.
items.anchor: at this revision, the local validation suite ran

items.label: Explicit gap
items.detail: The separate live-provider check has not run.
items.anchor: a separate live-provider check has not been run

items.label: Reproducible record
items.detail: Include the command and sanitized output.
items.anchor: Include the command and sanitized output

items.label: Safe screenshot
items.detail: Use fictional records for a private-list example.
items.anchor: If a screenshot shows a private list

conclusion.text: The reader should assess confidence without hidden context.
conclusion.anchor: a polished summary that hides gaps

scenes.title: Ask to see the observation
scenes.intro: Replace broad quality claims with specific evidence.

items.label: Reviewer
items.detail: Pair the standard with a concrete observation.
items.anchor: pair each important standard with a concrete observation

items.label: Instead of “handled”
items.detail: Show the failed-save test or code path.
items.anchor: rather than saying “errors are handled”

items.label: Instead of “secure”
items.detail: Name the access boundary, environment, and test limits.
items.anchor: Rather than saying “security is complete”

items.label: Confidence
items.detail: Mark claims that cannot be reproduced or inspected.
items.anchor: the reviewer cannot reproduce or inspect a claim

conclusion.text: You can ask for meaningful proof without reading every line of code.
conclusion.anchor: if you do not personally read the implementation
